[[Category:Artificial neural network]]
The '''model parameters''' of an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]], collectively denoted as $\theta$, are the [[artificial neuron#Mathematical_representation|'''weights''' and '''biases ''']] that connect individual [[artificial neuron]]s, learnt during [[#Training|traning]].

In general, parameters do not change while the model is in use. They are only adjusted during [[#Training|training]] between iterations.

== Definition ==

For an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]] of $N$ layers each with widths $d_0,\cdots,d_N$, the '''parameters'''

$$
\theta=\left\{\mathbf{W}^{(l)} \in\mathbb{R}^{d_l\times d_{l-1}},\vec b^{(l)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_l}\right\}_{l=1}^{N}.
$$

<blockquote>
'''Distinction from hyperparameters''': The '''[[hyperparameter]]s''' of an [[artificial neural network (ANN)]] determines its '''architecture''', while the '''parameters''' its '''behaviour'''.
</blockquote>

== Parameter count ==

$$
|\theta|=\sum_{l=1}^{N}\left(d_{l-1}d_l+d_l\right).
$$

== Training ==

With [[gradient descent]], training is the iteration with step

$$
\theta_{i+1}=\theta_i-\eta'\nabla_\theta L(\theta_i),
$$

<div class=center>
{| class="wikitable"
|-
| $\eta' \in \mathbb{R}$
| '''effective learning rate''', generally on the scale of $10^{-5}\to 10^{-3}$
|-
| $\nabla_\theta L(\theta_i)$
| the '''local gradient''' at $\theta_i$, determined via [[backpropagation]]
|}
</div> 

For a [[large language model (LLM)]], the loss function is generally [[language model loss]].
